Definition: from a presumed compound of G2372 and G3164; to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated:--be highly displeased.
BiblicalUsage: thymomachéō is the word the Bible uses when it means to be furiously angry with. In Acts 12:20, Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe to be furiously angry with still tells the truth about God, and I take it as it stands.
